standard_prerequisites.name: The universe of n-types
standard_prerequisites.statement: The type of n-types is the dependent pair of a type and a proof that it is an n-type, and the identity type of such a pair is equivalent to the type of equivalences between the underlying types because being an n-type is a mere proposition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose (n+1)-type property the counted theorem asserts, and its identity type is the first object analysed in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Embeddings and n-type-ness of function types
standard_prerequisites.statement: The projection from equivalences between X and X-prime to functions from X to X-prime is an embedding, and function types into an n-type are n-types.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof reduces the goal to the function type and then to the assumption that the target is an n-type.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractible types and the unit type
standard_prerequisites.statement: Any two contractible types are equivalent to the unit type and hence to each other, so the type of equivalences between them is inhabited.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the only content of the separate case n equal to minus two.

core_obligations: Unfold the goal: an identity type in the universe of n-types is an n-type, for any two of its elements (source line 224).
Replace that identity type by the type of equivalences between the underlying types, by the displayed observation retained as context (source line 225).

Use that the projection from equivalences to functions is an embedding, so that by the monotonicity result for n-types it suffices to show that the function type is an n-type, and conclude from the assumption that the target is an n-type (source lines 226-229).

Treat the case n equal to minus two separately: the equivalence type is a (-1)-type by the same argument and inhabited because contractible types are all equivalent to the unit type, so it is a (-2)-type, which is the claim for that case (source lines 231-233).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the identity type to the equivalence type by the retained observation.
Reduce equivalences to functions through the embedding projection, then to the target being an n-type.
The separate case n equal to minus two: inhabitedness upgrades the (-1)-type to a (-2)-type.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 220-222: the type of n-types is an (n+1)-type. The proof (source lines 223-234) is short but carries the whole argument and is not visible in the statement: it unfolds what an identity in the universe of n-types is, replaces it by the type of equivalences through the mere-proposition character of being an n-type, then chains two reductions, first through the embedding of equivalences into function types and then through the preservation of n-type-ness under arrow types, and finally treats the boundary case n equal to minus two, where the same argument gives a (-1)-type and inhabitedness of the equivalence type upgrades it to a (-2)-type. The two reduction steps and the boundary case are the substance; the statement alone shows none of them.
